## The one sentence to leave with

> **`break` leaves exactly one construct — the nearest enclosing loop or `switch`.**

Almost everything that goes wrong today is that sentence, not yet believed. You will meet
it again next week, when a `break` in the inner loop of a matrix search does not stop the
outer one.

## Act 1 · Drills — predict, then run (25 min)

```bash
./drill.sh --all
```

| Drills | Territory |
|---|---|
| `d01`–`d02` | the two classic `if` bugs: one equals sign, and an `else` that belongs to the wrong `if` |
| `d03`–`d04` | `switch`: fall-through with no `break`, and what `%2` does to a **negative** number |
| `d05`–`d07` | **`break` and `continue`, and where they actually land** |
| `d08`–`d10` | short-circuit `&&`, a ladder in the wrong order, and a `switch` that matches nothing |

::: {.callout-warning}
**`d07` never stops.** That is deliberate, and it is the point. Every drill run is capped
at five seconds so it cannot hang the machine — but predict *before* you run it, and look
carefully at where `i++` lives.
:::

A wrong prediction scores exactly as much as a right one — but only if you write it down
first.

## Act 2 · Fill the blanks (25 min)

| File | What it does |
|---|---|
| `b1_evenodd.c` | even or odd, with `if`/`else` — and it is tested on negatives |
| `b2_vowel.c` | vowel or consonant — a `switch` where **fall-through is the point**: five cases, one body |
| `b3_ticket.c` | ticket price by age bracket — an else-if **ladder** |
| `b4_grade.c` | a grade from marks — the same shape, built in the opposite direction |
| `b5_calc.c` | a mini calculator — `switch` on a character, every case with its own `break` |

::: {.callout-tip}
`b2` and `d03` use the same mechanism and reach opposite verdicts. In `d03` the missing
`break` is a **bug**; in `b2` the shared body is the **feature**. Be able to say why.
:::

## Act 3 · The checked three (40 min, solo)

| Problem | Task | Final line ends with exactly |
|---|---|---|
| `e1.c` | classify a triangle from three sides | `type=equilateral` \| `type=isosceles` \| `type=scalene` \| `type=invalid` |
| `e2.c` | is n prime? if not, its **smallest** divisor | `n=<N> prime` or `n=<N> divisor=<D>` |
| `e3.c` | a PIN, and three attempts | `access=granted tries=<N>` or `access=denied` |

`e1` — check **validity first**. Three lengths make a triangle only if every pair adds up
to more than the third: `5 5 8` is a triangle, `2 3 9` is three sticks that will not meet.
Then ask of your ladder: *do my cases cover every possibility?*

`e2` — search upward from 2 and **`break` the moment you find a divisor**; the spec asks
for the smallest, and there is no reason to keep looking. Then look at your upper limit:
going to `n-1` works, and stopping at `i*i <= n` also works — for 97 that is 9 passes
instead of 95. Add a counter and see.

`e3` — a loop that can end for **two different reasons**: the right PIN (you `break` out)
or the attempts running out (the condition ends it). After the loop, your program has to
know *which* happened. That is exactly what the two output lines are asking you to prove.

**How checking works** — `./check.sh e1` compiles *your source* and runs it on the public
examples **and on fresh random inputs drawn from the GIVEN**. A program that memorises an
example fails the next draw.

## Act 4 · Check, fix, bundle (10 min)

```bash
./check.sh
```

Fix, re-check, repeat. Then — green or time-up:

```bash
./check.sh --bundle
```

Carry `../lab05_<rolls>_<branch>_w<NN>.tar.gz` out with you (Moodle + email yourself).

## Stretch (fast finishers)

- **The bank menu.** A `while` loop showing a menu — balance, deposit, withdraw, quit —
  with a `switch` on the choice. Make `quit` actually quit. If your first attempt keeps
  looping, you have just rediscovered `d05` with your own hands, which is the best way to
  learn it.
- **Count the passes in `e2`.** Compare `i < n` against `i*i <= n` for n = 97 and n = 99.
- **Break `e1` on purpose.** Find three sides where your program says `scalene` but the
  right answer is `invalid`. Then explain why the order of your tests caused it.

## Reflect

✍️ Into `notes/answers.txt`: in `d05` the `break` ran and the loop kept going. In one
sentence — what exactly did that `break` leave?
